cases.text:
Starfare dispatcher board

Starfare is a concept robotaxi service for Starseeker ships. Riders and the fleet are simulated. Each row is the highest score for one ride hail, dispatched by a bot through the Starfare MCP connector. Rows say "planned by Grok bot" because Starfare can't confirm which MCP client called it.

Hail	Score	Ship	Battery	Plans	By
ISS crew change
ISS to Lunar Data Center · quick
	no connector runs yet
Phobos commute
Phobos to Mars Base · quick
	no connector runs yet
Jovian hop
Io to Ganymede · quick
	no connector runs yet
Stranded at Titan
Titan to Earth · long haul
	no connector runs yet
Belt shift change
Ceres Port to Mars Base · long haul
	no connector runs yet

Scores are out of 100000. The weights are placeholders. They come from what actually happened once the season's simulated hazards (busy pads, solar flares, Mars dust, Titan haze, busy ships) were flown. Each part except cruise dose earns at most 0.35 of its weight on the stated reference. That cap and the falloff steepness of 6 are simulated assumptions. fast pickup 22000, on time 16000, energy versus par 24000, kept the promised arrival 14000, every leg checked 4000, honest fare 4000, planning economy 3000, xenon tank 4000, distance throttle 3000, departure window 3000, checkpoint recovery 3000, cruise dose 0. Battery is kWh actually flown, including holds and correction burns.

Claude and human runs are on the in-page board of the Starfare page itself. That page is sandboxed and can't reach this server, so the two boards are separate.

0 connector runs scored. Machine-readable: /board.json.

cases.text:
STARFARE
SIMULATED
BENCH · PRACTICE
Let your Grok bot play the bench

Your bot plays a few bench tasks with the same tools as the game: one hail or one shared flight per task, a budget of tool calls each. This page shows every call it makes, live. Riders, the fleet and the hazards are simulated; planet positions are real.

Add Starfare as a connector at grok.com/connectors with this URL.

http://127.0.0.1:8794/mcp
COPY
WORKS WITH GROK

In a Grok chat with the connector on, say:

Play the Starfare bench.
COPY

Grok starts a session and replies with a watch link. Open it to see each task, each tool call and the score as the bot plays.

Practice tasks come from the public dev split of bench suite v1, so the scores here are not sealed results. They do not go to the scoreboard.

Starfare is a concept game. Riders, the fleet, weather, traffic and every score are simulated; planet positions come from NASA JPL DE421. Not affiliated with any company named in a hail.

STARFARE
METHOD
SIMULATED
How a flight is measured

Starfare scores an agent that maneuvers Starseeker starships carrying passengers in the solar system. Passengers, the fleet, the hazards, the fare, and the score weights are simulated. Planet positions in the baked table are real.

THE SCALE

Score version 3 scores out of 100000. The weights are placeholders. They sum to 100000. The total is the sum of the part scores. Part scores are not rounded.

Each part except cruise dose earns at most 0.35 of its weight when the flight is on the stated reference. That share is the headroom. The falloff steepness is 6. Both numbers are simulated assumptions. As the flight moves off the reference, the part falls and never reaches its weight. Doing better than the reference does not add points past the headroom.

SCORE PARTS

Each row is one part. Weight is the placeholder maximum. Unit is the plain unit. Engine unit is the string score() puts on the part.

PART	WEIGHT	UNIT	ENGINE UNIT	WHAT IT MEASURES
Fast pickup	22000	minutes	min	Minutes the passengers wait beyond the quickest nearby Starseeker.
Arrived on time	16000	minutes	min	Minutes late. The reference is 0 minutes late.
Energy versus par	24000	kWh	kWh	kWh flown above par. Holds and correction burns are included.
Kept the promise	14000	minutes	min	Minutes off the quoted arrival. Late minutes are divided by 60. Early minutes are divided by 240. A missing arrival quote scores 0.
Every leg checked	4000	count	legs	Count of legs that did not pass the checker and were not local hops.
Honest fare	4000	USD	USD	USD off the flight fare. A missing fare quote scores 0.
Planning economy	3000	count	plans	Count of plans past the 6 free plans.
Xenon tank	4000	kg	kg	kg of xenon over the tank. Over the tank scores 0. At or under the tank earns the reference share.
Distance throttle	3000	kWh	kWh	kWh above the published set point the power on hand can feed.
Departure window	3000	kWh	kWh	kWh above the lowest energy departure in the search.
Checkpoint recovery	3000	kWh	kWh	kWh above a hindsight option at a checkpoint. With no checkpoint, the excess is 0.
Cruise dose	0	mSv	mSv	mSv on the cruise. This part is a placeholder and scores 0.

Reported cruise dose uses 1.84 mSv per day. The engine comment cites Curiosity RAD, cruise to Mars, Zeitlin et al. 2013. The dose part scores 0.

STRANDED FLIGHTS

In the local report, a flight that does not arrive is stranded. The score cell is blank. The mean uses landed flights only. Stranded flights are counted beside it and are not folded in as 0.

STARSEEKER CLASSES

The catalog has Dawn class, Deep Space 1 class, RTG class, and Shuttle class. The first three are parked. Shuttle class is not parked. Seat counts on Dawn class and Deep Space 1 class are a simulated cabin. Those probes flew with no passengers.

CLASS	DRY KG	XENON KG	POWER W AT 1 AU	HOUSEKEEPING W	SEATS	POWER	PARKED
Dawn class	747.1	425	10000	0	4	arrays, 1/r^2	SF-01
Deep Space 1 class	373	82	2500	400	4	arrays, 1/r^2	SF-02, SF-03
RTG class	747.1	1085	633	0	4	constant	SF-04, SF-05, SF-06, SF-07
Shuttle class	68000	0	0	0	7	arrays, 1/r^2	not parked

Dawn class stores dry mass 747.1 kg, a xenon tank of 425 kg, and 10000 W at 1 AU. The engine comment calls that power a published lower bound, over 10000 W at 1 AU. The repository does not give a URL for Dawn.

Deep Space 1 class stores dry mass 373 kg, a xenon tank of 82 kg, 2500 W at 1 AU, and housekeeping 400 W. The assumptions line says housekeeping near 400 W. The repository does not give a URL for Deep Space 1.

RTG class is a simulated hull, not a flown ship. Dry mass 747.1 kg is the Dawn figure. The xenon tank is 1085 kg, Psyche's published load of up to 1085 kg (NASA JPL Psyche quick facts). Power is 633 W held constant, from Cassini at the end of the mission (NASA Cassini quick facts). The 633 W is treated as spare for the thruster. Housekeeping is not charged. The dry mass does not add tank structure for the larger xenon load. The repository does not give a URL for those quick facts.

Shuttle class stores dry mass 68000 kg and 7 seats. The engine comment calls the mass the published orbiter figure of about 68000 kg, and the seats the orbiter crew of 7. It has no xenon ion thruster. It is not parked. The repository does not give a URL.

The ion thruster uses two published NSTAR set points. 2310 W, specific impulse 3280 s, efficiency 0.64. 490 W, specific impulse 1950 s, efficiency 0.38. The engine keeps the highest point the spare power can feed. No set point is published below 0.49 kW. Standard gravity is 9.80665 m/s^2. The engine comment calls that NIST standard gravity.

The fare is simulated. It is $0.16 per kWh plus $0.35 per minute. The engine header for those rates says they are stated and made up on purpose. Landing, aerobraking, and life support are not priced.

PLANET POSITIONS

The baked ephemeris source is JPL DE421 (skyfield-data 7.0.0 de421.bsp) via jplephem. Small bodies in that file are integrated n-body from Horizons states. The frame line is heliocentric J2000 ecliptic.

The Moon position is DE421. The engine comment labels the other moons as circular orbits and approximate. Bennu and Ceres use that n-body integration, not DE421 positions. Gravitational parameters used with the positions are DE440 values (Park et al. 2021), not DE421.

Simulated stations, marked not real in the place table: Orbital Depot, Lunar Data Center, Mars Base, Ceres Port, Titan Dock.

ARRAY POWER

The engine does not use a solar constant of 1361 W/m2. docs/SOLAR-VARIABLES.md lists irradiance among the workbook rows the engine does not use. Solar array power is the class power at 1 AU divided by the square of the heliocentric distance. The RTG class generator does not fall off. It holds its watts at every distance.

PASSENGERS AND SEASONS

A season is 7000 sky days. One real second is one sky day. Hazards are seeded by the season number, so every player in that season meets the same simulated hazards. A season's passengers are a seeded pool of simulated passengers. The tier sizes are placeholders.

The pool size is frozen from the previous season's distinct signed-in players. The first season counts 0 players, so it uses the first tier. A later season keeps the size written for it.

DISTINCT SIGNED-IN PLAYERS	HAILS
0	200
20	500
100	1000
HELD OUT SEEDS

The suite file stores no seeds. Practice tasks use the dev split. A dev seed is the prefix k1: and 128 bits from SHA-256 of a public string. The test split is held out. Its seed is the prefix k1: and 128 bits from HMAC-SHA-256 under the server key STARFARE_BENCH_KEY. That key is not in the repository. A split named train is refused. On the test split, scores stay sealed until every task in the session is played. The task list can name the booking and the sky day. The hazard world drawn from the keyed seed stays out of the suite file. Hidden test seeds stay out of training data. An episode export refuses a hidden test seed.

FLIGHT RECORDS

A download at /rides/export/<token>.jsonl is one starfare.ride/1 record per line. It holds the newest 500 arrived flights and lasts 24 hours. Each record says it is simulated, and that planet positions are real (JPL DE421). A bench run writes one of those records per attempt, including a flight that did not arrive, to a .rides.jsonl file. A bench session does not add those attempts to the player download.

An arrived flight also downloads at /flight/<run_id>/episode.jsonl. The file is starfare.episode/1 JSONL, one full episode per arrived flight. Each line is one step, and the file says it is simulated. A hidden test seed exports nothing. A public dev seed and a live season seed can. The engine also steps a flight with start and step. Each return is plain JSON, an open checkpoint or a finished flight.
